- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if price is falling below 70.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward 70–75 range after 3+ consecutive high values, reduce forecast slope; apply downward bias of 1–3% per day.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 1.00, 0.33), model often misreads momentum; use 2-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70 after 10+ days of high prices, model overcorrects; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1–2% for next 3 days.
